title: Joshua Angrist turned lotteries and birth dates into natural experiments, and won the Nobel Prize in Economics

trailer.text: Joshua Angrist, an economist and professor at MIT, won the 2021 Nobel Prize in Economics together with David Card and Guido Imbens.
According to Wikipedia, he was born to a Jewish family in Ohio, and according to ISRAEL21c, he holds American and Israeli citizenship.
Many questions in the social sciences concern cause and effect, and they are difficult to answer because there is nothing to use as a comparison.
The laureates showed that it is possible to answer them using natural experiments, real-life situations that resemble a randomised experiment.
According to the Nobel Committee, their work revolutionised empirical research in the social sciences.

glance.label: Citizenship
glance.value: American and Israeli, according to ISRAEL21c

stations.title: A boy from Pittsburgh, a paratrooper in the IDF

paragraphs.text: According to the Swedish Academy, Angrist was born in 1960 in Columbus, Ohio.
According to Wikipedia, he was born to a Jewish family and raised in Pittsburgh.
According to MIT Technology Review, he left high school after the eleventh grade, having completed the minimum requirements.
According to The Tech, after his bachelor's degree he moved to Israel, became a citizen and began graduate studies.
According to Wikipedia, he lived in Israel from 1982 to 1985 and served as a paratrooper in the Israel Defense Forces.
According to The Tech, he left his studies, served two years in the Israeli army, and returned to the United States to complete them at Princeton.
According to the Academy, he received a Ph.D. from Princeton in 1989.

stations.title: A question with no comparison group

paragraphs.text: Many questions in the social sciences concern cause and effect.
They are difficult to answer, because we have nothing to use as a comparison.
According to the Nobel Committee, it is not possible to conduct a randomised experiment determining who attends upper-secondary school and who does not.
According to MIT Technology Review, it is also not possible to assign students to schools randomly in order to test their effect.
Comparing scores between schools can be misleading, because top districts may attract families with better-prepared students.
Therefore, according to the magazine, Angrist relies on natural experiments.
The Nobel Committee described natural experiments as situations that arise in real life and resemble randomised experiments.

stations.title: The draft lottery and the quarter of birth

paragraphs.text: According to The Tech, in 1990 Angrist used the Vietnam-era draft lottery to estimate the effect of military service on lifetime earnings.
According to MIT Technology Review, he found that white men who were drafted and served in the early 1970s earned about 15 percent less in the early 1980s.
According to the Nobel Committee, Angrist worked with his colleague Alan Krueger, now deceased, on a landmark article that showed how the effect of years of education on income can be examined.
In the United States, children may leave school at age 16 or 17, depending on the state.
Angrist and Krueger compared people born in the first quarter of the year with those born in the fourth quarter.
They found that the first group had spent less time in education.
According to the Nobel Committee, the causal effect they found was stronger than the association between education and income, which amounted to seven percent, and this was surprising.
According to MIT Technology Review, the paper they published in 1991 is considered a textbook example of a natural experiment.

stations.title: A new framework with Guido Imbens

paragraphs.text: In the mid-1990s, Angrist and Imbens solved a methodological problem.
They showed how precise conclusions about cause and effect can be drawn from natural experiments.
According to Angrist's CV, their paper on the local average treatment effect was published in Econometrica in March 1994.

According to MIT Technology Review, the paper formalized the idea that the average effect of a policy is best measured by its influence on people who otherwise would not have been exposed to the circumstances it encouraged.
Econometrics expert Whitney Newey said that this is probably one of the best papers in econometrics over a span of a decade, according to the magazine.
According to MIT Technology Review, Angrist did not invent the quasi-experimental methods.
They spread from the eighties onward through a group of prominent economists, among them Alan Krueger.
Angrist taught in the Department of Economics at the Hebrew University as a senior lecturer in the early 1990s.
In 1994 he served on the Israeli Finance Ministry's Working Group on Israeli-Palestinian Labor Market Relations.
According to MIT Technology Review, classes in Israel are capped at 40 students, and Angrist and Lavy used this to examine the effect of class size.
They found that smaller classes produced significant gains in math and reading among fifth-graders.
Prof. Victor Lavy of the Hebrew University said that Angrist is a loyal friend of the State of Israel.
According to The Tech, Angrist joined the MIT faculty in 1996, and he has been the Ford Professor of Economics since 2008.
According to MIT Technology Review, he built a kind of virtual laboratory of economics, in which he generates precise answers to difficult social questions.
He relies only on empirical data that illuminate causal relationships in society.
According to MIT Technology Review, in 2011 Angrist, together with David Autor and Parag Pathak, launched the School Effectiveness and Inequality Initiative (SEII).
According to The Tech, Angrist said that some applicants to charter schools are admitted by lottery, and that this turns out to be the key, because it contains an element of random assignment.
According to MIT Technology Review, a 2009 report found that certain Boston charter schools produced an average gain of roughly 15 percentile points on middle-school math exams.
Soon after the research was released, the governor of Massachusetts and the mayor of Boston adopted more charter-friendly positions.
Angrist himself thinks charter schools are too different from one another to justify sweeping conclusions, according to the magazine.
According to MIT Technology Review, Esther Duflo, whom Angrist advised, said that his focus on selection bias spurred her to conduct field experiments.
David Autor said that Angrist managed to answer questions that others did not think could be answered empirically.

According to the magazine, as of the August before the article was published, Angrist was among the 100 most-cited economists in the world, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, which holds data on more than 33,000 authors.
According to The Tech, he doubted that data and AI tools are revolutionizing econometrics, noting that these tools are rarely central.
The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences decided to award the 2021 Nobel Prize in Economics to David Card, Joshua Angrist and Guido Imbens.
The laureates showed that it is possible to answer questions of cause and effect using natural experiments.
The chair of the prize committee said that their research substantially improved the ability to answer key causal questions, to the great benefit of society.

According to the Academy, Angrist and Imbens's framework fundamentally changed how researchers approach empirical questions examined with data from natural experiments or randomized field experiments.
According to the Nobel Committee, it has been widely adopted by researchers who work with observational data.
Clarifying the assumptions necessary to establish a causal relationship increased the transparency and credibility of empirical research.
The prize amount is 10 million Swedish kronor, with one half to Card and the other half jointly to Angrist and Imbens.
According to the Academy, Card's studies showed, among other things, that increasing the minimum wage does not necessarily lead to fewer jobs.
According to the Nobel Committee, in the early 1990s the conventional view among economists was that a high minimum wage reduces employment.
According to NBER, all three laureates were affiliated with the NBER Labor Studies Program, which Card directed for nearly a decade.
According to ISRAEL21c, Angrist is the 13th Israeli to win the Nobel Prize and the third in economics.
According to The Tech, he is the eighth MIT faculty member to win the Nobel Prize in Economics.
According to his CV, in June 2022 he received an honorary doctorate from Oberlin, and in April 2023 he was elected to the National Academy of Sciences.
Card said that one of the secrets of Angrist's success is his tenacity.
According to MIT Technology Review, some economists found pure empiricism foreign to them, and younger economists working in Angrist's mode drew criticism.
According to the magazine, a 2007 article in the New Republic decried the “academic parlor game” of new scholars using natural experiments.

In an interview with MIT Technology Review, Angrist said that in the ten years before the interview there had been criticism that he, his students and his school of thought were concerned with tools and not with questions, and added that in his view this is not fair.
He considered this unfair.

disagreements.question: How much does an additional year of education add to income, according to Angrist and Krueger?

versions.says: MIT Technology Review: about 7.5 percent more in annual earnings

disagreements.question: Until what year was Angrist a senior lecturer at the Hebrew University?
What amount was shared by Angrist and Imbens?

versions.says: ISRAEL21c: the two share half of the prize money, stated as $1.14 million
Wikipedia: the two received half of 10 million Swedish kronor, which is $1.14 million, and the rest went to Card

disagreements.question: When was the minimum wage increase in New Jersey studied?

versions.says: Nobel Committee: the hourly minimum wage in New Jersey was increased on 1 April 1992, from 4.25 to 5.05 dollars
The Tech: Card studied employment in fast food establishments in New Jersey and Pennsylvania in 1993, after the increase

claims.text: שאלות רבות במדעי החברה עוסקות בסיבה ותוצאה, וקשה לענות עליהן כי אין לנו דבר שישמש להשוואה.

claims.text: ועדת הנובל תיארה ניסויים טבעיים כמצבים המתרחשים בחיים האמיתיים ומזכירים ניסויים אקראיים.

claims.text: לפי ועדת הנובל, אנגריסט עבד עם עמיתו אלן קרוגר (שנפטר) במאמר דרך שהראה כיצד אפשר לבחון את השפעת שנות לימוד על הכנסה.
claims.quote: Joshua Angrist and his colleague Alan Krueger (now deceased) showed how this could be done in a landmark article.

claims.text: באמצע שנות ה-90 פתרו אנגריסט ואימבנס בעיה מתודולוגית והראו כיצד אפשר להסיק מסקנות מדויקות על סיבה ותוצאה מניסויים טבעיים.

claims.text: לפי ועדת הנובל, הבהרת ההנחות הדרושות לביסוס קשר סיבתי הגבירה את השקיפות והאמינות של מחקר אמפירי.
claims.quote: By clarifying the assumptions necessary to establish a causal relationship, their framework has also increased the transparency

claims.text: סכום הפרס הוא 10 מיליון כתר שוודי, מחציתו לקארד והמחצית השנייה במשותף לאנגריסט ולאימבנס.
claims.quote: Prize amount: 10 million Swedish kronor, with one half to David Card and the other half jointly to Joshua Angrist and Guido Imbens.

claims.text: לפי האקדמיה, מחקרי קארד הראו בין השאר שהעלאת שכר המינימום אינה מובילה בהכרח לפחות משרות.
claims.quote: The results showed, among other things, that increasing the minimum wage does not necessarily lead to fewer jobs.

claims.text: לפי ועדת הנובל, בראשית שנות ה-90 הדעה המקובלת בקרב כלכלנים הייתה ששכר מינימום גבוה מפחית תעסוקה.
claims.quote: In the early 1990s, the conventional wisdom among economists was that higher minimum wages lead to lower employment because they increase wage costs for businesses.

claims.text: לפי NBER, שלושת הזוכים היו שותפים בתוכנית לימודי העבודה של NBER, שקארד ניהל כמעט עשור.
claims.quote: All three were affiliated with the NBER Labor Studies Program, which Card directed for nearly a decade.

claims.text: לפי ISRAEL21c, אנגריסט הוא הישראלי ה-13 שזוכה בנובל והשלישי בכלכלה.
claims.quote: Now he has become the 13th Israeli to win the coveted award, and the third to win it in economics.

claims.text: לפי The Tech, אנגריסט הוא חבר הסגל השמיני של MIT שזוכה בנובל בכלכלה.
claims.quote: Angrist is the eighth MIT faculty member to win the Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences.

claims.text: לפי קורות החיים של אנגריסט, הוא נבחר לחבר באקדמיה הלאומית למדעים באפריל 2023 וקיבל תואר דוקטור לשם כבוד מאוברלין ביוני 2022.
claims.quote: Elected Member, National Academy of Sciences, April 2023. Honorary Degrees, Oberlin College, June 2022

claims.text: קארד אמר שאחד הסודות להצלחתו של אנגריסט הוא עקשנותו.
claims.quote: One of the secrets of his success is his tenacity

claims.text: לפי MIT Technology Review, חלק מהכלכלנים מצאו אמפיריציזם טהור זר, וכלכלנים צעירים העובדים בדרכו של אנגריסט ספגו ביקורת.
claims.quote: some younger economists working in the mode of Angrist, Card, and Krueger have drawn criticism

claims.text: לפי MIT Technology Review, מאמר ב-New Republic מ-2007 גינה את "משחק הסלון האקדמי" של חוקרים חדשים העושים שימוש בניסויים טבעיים.
claims.quote: A 2007 article in the New Republic decried the “academic parlor game” played by new scholars using natural experiments.

claims.text: אנגריסט אמר שהייתה התנגדות בעשור האחרון לטענה שהוא ותלמידיו עוסקים בכלים ולא בשאלות, וסבר שזה לא הוגן.
claims.quote: There has been some pushback in the last 10 years, that guys like me, or my students, or my school of thought—that we’re all about the tools and not about the questions

claims.text: לפי ועדת הנובל, אנגריסט וקרוגר מצאו שהשפעתה של שנת לימוד נוספת על ההכנסה היא תשעה אחוזים.
claims.quote: the effect of an additional year of education on income was nine per cent

claims.text: לפי MIT Technology Review, אנגריסט וקרוגר מצאו ששנת לימוד נוספת שווה כ-7.5 אחוזים יותר בשכר שנתי.
claims.quote: an additional year of education was worth about 7.5 percent more in annual earnings

claims.text: לפי ISRAEL21c, אנגריסט יתחלק עם אימבנס במחצית מסכום הפרס, שצוין כ-1.14 מיליון דולר.
claims.quote: He will share half the $1.14 million prize money with Imbens for their

claims.text: לפי ויקיפדיה, השניים קיבלו מחצית מסכום הפרס של 10 מיליון כתר שוודי (1.14 מיליון דולר), והשאר הלך לקארד.
claims.quote: The two men received one-half of the prize money of 10 million Swedish crowns ($1.14 million U.S.)

claims.text: לפי ועדת הנובל, ב-1 באפריל 1992 הועלה שכר המינימום השעתי בניו ג'רזי מ-4.25 ל-5.05 דולר.
claims.quote: 1 April 1992: The hourly minimum wage in New Jersey was increased from 4.25 dollars to 5.05 dollars.

claims.text: לפי The Tech, קארד חקר תעסוקה במסעדות מזון מהיר בניו ג'רזי ובפנסילבניה ב-1993, לאחר העלאת שכר המינימום בניו ג'רזי.
claims.quote: Card studied employment in fast food establishments in New Jersey and Pennsylvania in 1993, on the heels of a minimum wage hike in New Jersey
